description: Persistent Collections (M8/M8a) - Add persistent vectors (RRB) and maps (HAMT) to JACL with construction, access, update, iteration, structural equality, and print support. Includes design fixes: split map/transform, vec-set growth semantics, and cached structural hashing for collections-as-keys.

userStories.title: Vector constructor and basic accessors

[vec-len $v] returns the number of elements as an i32

userStories.title: Eager node-level structural hashing for RRB vector
userStories.description: As a library developer, I want every RRB vector node to maintain an eagerly-updated structural hash so that the root hash is always available in O(1) and vectors work correctly as map keys.
acceptanceCriteria: RV_LEAF gains a uint32_t hash field — the rotate-XOR of its element hashes: hash ^= rotate_left(element_hash_fn(elem[i]), i % 32) for each slot i
RV_INTERNAL gains a uint32_t hash field — the XOR of its children's hash fields
RV_ROOT gains a uint32_t hash field — XOR of tree root node hash and tail node hash (or just tail hash if tree is NULL)
element_hash_fn is a function pointer uint32_t (*)(RRB_VEC_T) stored via a RV_SET_HASH_HANDLER(fn) call (similar to HAMT's key handler pattern), so the library stays generic
Hashes are computed eagerly: every RV_COPY_LEAF, RV_COPY_INTERNAL, and RV_MK_ROOT recomputes the hash from its children/elements at construction time
Path-copying on push_back/set naturally propagates hash updates — only the O(log n) copied nodes recompute
RV_HASH(root) is a simple field read returning root->hash in O(1)
rotate_left is a bitwise left rotation: (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n))

New tests added to lib/rrb_vec/test_rrb_vec.c (or a new test_rrb_vec_hash.c): verify hash is consistent across equal vectors built different ways, verify hash changes when elements change, verify hash differs for permuted elements (rotate-XOR order-dependence), verify empty vector hash is deterministic
If a new test file is created, add it to the TESTS array in build.sh
build.sh gains a --lib flag that runs only the lib/ tests (all entries with src paths starting with lib/). Running build.sh with no args still runs everything
All existing RRB vec tests still pass
Template instantiation in src/collections.c still compiles cleanly
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g

userStories.title: Eager node-level structural hashing for HAMT
userStories.description: As a library developer, I want every HAMT node to maintain an eagerly-updated structural hash so that the map hash is always available in O(1) via root->hash and maps work correctly as map keys.
acceptanceCriteria: H_NODE base struct gains a uint32_t hash field for structural content hash — accessible uniformly on any node type
H_LEAF structural hash (header.hash) is computed as key_hash_fn(key) ^ val_hash_fn(value), distinct from existing key hash field used for trie navigation
H_INTERNAL structural hash (header.hash) is the XOR of its children's header.hash fields
H_COLLISION structural hash (header.hash) is the XOR of its items' header.hash fields
XOR combining is order-independent, which is correct for maps since two equal maps may have different internal trie structure
key_hash_fn and val_hash_fn are function pointers stored via H_SET_HASH_HANDLERS(key_fn, val_fn) call, so the library stays generic
Hashes are computed eagerly: every node allocation/copy recomputes from children at construction time
Path-copying on set/unset naturally propagates hash updates — only the O(log n) copied nodes recompute
H_NODE_HASH(node) accessor returns node->hash (or 0 for NULL)
No H_ROOT wrapper — hash is accessed directly via root->hash, avoiding extra indirection

New tests added in lib/hamt/test_hamt_hash.c: verify hash is consistent for maps with same entries inserted in different order, verify hash changes when entries change, verify empty map hash is 0, verify collision node hashing, verify transient consistency
test_hamt_hash.c added to the TESTS array in build.sh
All existing HAMT tests still pass
Template instantiation in src/collections.c still compiles cleanly
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
userStories.notes: H_ROOT wrapper dropped per user direction — unnecessary indirection since root->hash provides O(1) access directly

userStories.title: Wire cached hashes into jacl_val_hash for collections-as-keys
userStories.description: As a JACL developer, I want jacl_val_hash to use the cached structural hashes from vectors and maps so that collections work correctly as map keys.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_val_hash for JACL_TAG_VECTOR calls jacl_vec_hash(root) — O(1) field read from RRB root
jacl_val_hash for JACL_TAG_MAP reads root->hash via jacl_map_node_hash(root) — O(1) field read from HAMT root node
collections__init() calls RV_SET_HASH_HANDLER(jacl_val_hash) and H_SET_HASH_HANDLERS(jacl_val_hash, jacl_val_hash) to wire in the element/key/value hash functions
jacl_val_eq for JACL_TAG_VECTOR and JACL_TAG_MAP delegates to deep structural equality (existing vm__deep_eq logic or equivalent)
[map-get [map [vec 1] "a"] [vec 1]] returns "a" — structurally equal vectors as keys find same entry
[map-get [map [map "x" 1] "nested"] [map "x" 1]] returns "nested" — maps as keys work
[eq] still uses structural equality (verify no regression)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: No H_ROOT wrapper — HAMT root is still H_NODE*, hash accessed directly via root->hash
